# restate_cloud_byoc_region_access (Resource)

Who may reach the entry point of an AWS Managed BYOC region built with a region grant: the IPv4 networks that may connect to its load balancer directly, and an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service for private connections from your own VPCs. The region must be `ACTIVE`.

The resource sets the region's whole access setting, so an argument left out returns to its default: every address is admitted, and there is no endpoint service. Manage one `restate_cloud_byoc_region_access` for each region. Two of them for the same region overwrite each other. Destroying the resource returns the region to those defaults.

Restricting `entry_source_cidrs` also keeps out Restate's control plane. While a list is set, Restate collects no usage from the region's environments, and the Cloud Console's environment views work only from an allowed network. Restate's own AWS account is always allowed to connect to an enabled endpoint service, and no argument changes that.

Once you enable `private_link`, the apply waits until AWS has created the endpoint service, so `endpoint_service_name` is known to resources that use it in the same apply, such as an `aws_vpc_endpoint`. The wait is bounded by the `create` or `update` timeout. If it runs out during a create, the setting stays in effect at Restate and nothing is recorded in the state, so the next apply sends the same setting again and keeps waiting.

This resource needs a Restate Cloud control plane that offers `SetRegionAccess`. Where it does not, the apply fails with a message that says so.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Private-only access to an AWS region: no address reaches the load balancer directly, and the
# listed AWS account may connect through an interface endpoint.
#
# An empty entry_source_cidrs also keeps out Restate's control plane, so Restate collects no usage
# from the region's environments, and the Cloud Console's environment views stop working from
# outside your network. Leave the argument out to admit every address.
resource "restate_cloud_byoc_region_access" "production_eu" {
  region_id = restate_cloud_byoc_region.production_eu.id

  entry_source_cidrs = []

  private_link = {
    enabled            = true
    allowed_principals = ["arn:aws:iam::210987654321:root"]
  }

  # The apply waits until AWS has created the endpoint service, within the create timeout.
  timeouts {
    create = "30m"
  }
}

# Known in the same apply, so an aws_vpc_endpoint in your own configuration can use it as its
# service_name. The managed BYOC guide shows one.
output "restate_endpoint_service_name" {
  value = restate_cloud_byoc_region_access.production_eu.endpoint_service_name
}

output "restate_endpoint_availability_zone_ids" {
  value = restate_cloud_byoc_region_access.production_eu.availability_zone_ids
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `region_id` (String) The AWS Managed BYOC region to set the access of, for example `restate_cloud_byoc_region.<name>.id`. Referencing it makes the resource wait until the region is `ACTIVE`, and makes a destroy reset the access before the region is deleted. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `entry_source_cidrs` (Set of String) The IPv4 networks that may reach the region's load balancer directly, such as `203.0.113.0/24`. Each must be a network address with no host bits set and no leading zeros, and at most 10 are allowed.

Leave it out to admit every address. An empty set admits no client directly, so the region is reached only through `private_link`. Traffic through an endpoint carries no consumer address, so this list does not apply to it.
- `private_link` (Attributes) A VPC endpoint service on the region's load balancer, so that the listed principals can connect through interface endpoints. Leave it out for a region with no endpoint service. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--private_link))
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `account_id` (String) Account the region belongs to.
- `availability_zone_ids` (Set of String) The zones the endpoint service covers, as zone IDs such as `euc1-az1`. Zone names differ between AWS accounts, so match the subnets of an interface endpoint by zone ID. Null while `private_link` is off.
- `endpoint_service_name` (String) The name to give an interface endpoint, `com.amazonaws.vpce.<region>.vpce-svc-<id>`. Null while `private_link` is off. Use it as `service_name` of an `aws_vpc_endpoint`.
- `endpoint_service_state` (String) The state AWS reports for the endpoint service, such as `Available`. Null while `private_link` is off.
- `id` (String) The region ID.

<a id="nestedatt--private_link"></a>
### Nested Schema for `private_link`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the region has an endpoint service. With `false`, the region has none, and the other arguments are kept only in the configuration.

Optional:

- `acceptance_required` (Boolean) Whether each connection request waits until Restate accepts it. Defaults to `false`.
- `allowed_principals` (Set of String) The IAM principals that may connect an interface endpoint to the service: `arn:aws:iam::<12-digit account>:root`, `...:role/<name>` or `...:user/<name>`, at most 20. Restate's own AWS account is always allowed and cannot be listed.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The access of a BYOC region is imported by account ID and region ID together.
terraform import restate_cloud_byoc_region_access.production_eu acc_1a2b3c/rgn_a1b2c3d4e5
```
